conviction_note: The findings sum to +1.0. They are small positives on the Q4 guide: the display-glass price hike and a promised new margin target. Against them sits a mild negative from the October AI-basket tape. The scaled number is (2*0.52-1)*8.0 = +0.32. p_up sits barely above 50 because this name has sold four straight beats (-3.3, -5.0, -8.9, -12.1). The July sell-off came after a 46% drawdown, so a washed-out tape has not protected it before. The two measurements agree in sign, and the scaled one is smaller because the reaction history pulls p_up to 50 rather than shrinking the findings twice.
bar: Q3 2026 core sales $4.9-5.0B and core EPS $0.85-0.89 (company guide, Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000253/glw-20260728xex99xq22026.htm). So the Q3 bar sits at or just above the top of the guide, and the CFO pre-signalled that level on 2026-09-09. The Q4 bar is NOT directly sourced. Implied Q4 EPS is about $0.92 (FY26 consensus $3.28 less Q1 $0.70, Q2 $0.78 and Q3 consensus $0.88), so the guidance findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 16,842,925 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 2.17 days to cover (equibles, FINRA-derived, https://equibles.com/stocks/glw/shortinterest). That is about 2% of roughly 860M shares, down from 20.0M at 2026-08-31; the 10-15 settlement is not yet published. Not a crowded short, so no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25d skew +3.99 vol points (puts bid), put/call OI 1.01, event-implied move 6.62% (straddle 8.52%), spot 127.70, -15.76% over 20d, -3.8% over 5d, -50% from the 52w high ($255.69 close on 2026-06-29). The stock fell about 19% in October, inside an AI-infrastructure rout (Nasdaq -2.1% on 2026-10-16 on CoreWeave debt worries and TSMC's cautious 2027 note) and an 8.3% drop on 2026-10-22 (JPM target cut to $165, Neutral). Earnings-day reactions have been negative four times running, all on beats.

findings.finding: At Citi TMT on 2026-09-09 the CFO said Q3 is 'running really well' and Corning reaches a $20B annualized run rate in Q3, i.e. Q3 core sales of about $5.0B, at the high end of or slightly above the $4.9-5.0B guide. Consensus already sits at $5.02B / $0.88, so the likely print is a modest beat (Q2 beat revenue by about 2.6%, $4.74B vs $4.62B) of roughly 1% on revenue and $0.01-0.02 on EPS, inside what management told the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Corning has beaten EPS five quarters running and fell on each of the last four prints (2025-10-28 -3.29%, 2026-01-28 -4.98%, 2026-04-28 -8.9%, 2026-07-28 -12.1%). Q2 2026 beat revenue by $0.12B and EPS by $0.03 and the stock fell 12.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. Consensus moved to $5.02B, above the top of the guide, after the CFO's remarks. If it were unpriced, consensus would sit at the $4.95B midpoint. Only the size of any overshoot beyond $5.0B is open.
findings.independence: Investing.com summary of the same Citi appearance (https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/corning-at-citis-2026-global-tmt-conference-ai-demand-lifts-outlook-93CH-4458174). Same event, so it counts once.

findings.finding: The CFO said on 2026-09-09 that Q4 will be 'bigger than the third quarter' with high-teens YoY growth continuing into Q4 and 2027, and EPS growing faster than sales. On the Q4 2025 core-sales base of $4.41B, high-teens means a Q4 guide of about $5.16-5.24B. Implied Q4 EPS consensus is about $0.92 (+28% YoY), which matches what the CFO signalled, so an in-line Q4 guide is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 guide given 2026-07-28 implied about 16% growth vs Q2's 17%, was read as deceleration, and the stock fell 12.1% despite management saying there was 'no implied message' about Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the CFO said it publicly. Q4 2025 base from https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260127020453/en. The open question is whether the guide reads as 'about 20%' acceleration (Q2 call language) or high-teens. Either side is a several-point move on this name, so I size it at 0 with a wide band.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 call transcript has the CFO saying growth should 'accelerate toward about 20%' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-corning-beats-q2-2026-estimates-but-shares-sink-93CH-4817120). That is a different event and the same speaker.

findings.finding: Corning is raising yen-priced display glass substrate prices by '15% or more' globally, effective Q4 2026 (Counterpoint Research, 2026-10-07), citing yen depreciation and raw material, precious metal, energy and logistics costs. Corning hedges its yen in core results, so a yen-denominated price rise flows largely to core sales and margin in the Q4 guide. On roughly $1B a quarter of display revenue inside the $1.46B Glass Innovations segment, phased in, that could be tens of millions of dollars and a few cents of EPS above an otherwise high-teens Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2023 (20%) and 2024 display price increases supported Glass/Display results. This stock has traded on optical rather than display, so a display-driven upside has historically been a secondary line.
findings.why_not_priced: This is industry research, not a Corning press release, and it came after the CFO's 2026-09-09 Q4 comments. Implied Q4 EPS consensus (about $0.92) equals what the CFO's pre-hike framing implies. If it were priced, Q4 estimates would sit above the CFO's high-teens/EPS-faster-than-sales arithmetic. The display share of revenue, the phasing and the size are my inference, and the Q4 bar is unsourced, so the size is capped.
findings.independence: A separate industry repost dates the announcement to September 2026 and says panel makers TCL CSOT, BOE and HKC issued pricing notices downstream (https://www.smbom.com/news/51292). That is a different outlet, possibly the same underlying Corning notice.

findings.finding: On the Q2 2026 call management said operating margin should stay at or above 20% with 'a new target to come later this year'. The CFO said 2026-09-09 that the 20% target was reached early. The Q3 print is the next scheduled venue for a new margin target or a Springboard update; JPMorgan says Q3 may be too early for material Springboard updates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Springboard upgrade on 2026-07-28 ($40B by 2030) came with the 12.1% fall. Target raises have not by themselves lifted this stock on print day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is uncertain whether the update comes at this print or at a later event. A higher margin target would directly lift 2027 EPS estimates ($4.29 consensus), which are not yet above the 20% margin path. If it were priced, the 2027 consensus would already embed above-20% margins.
findings.independence: Investing.com preview of 2026-10-26 cites JPMorgan that Q3 may be too early for material Springboard updates (https://investing.com/news/earnings/all-eyes-on-corning-earnings-as-ai-fiber-growth-faces-test-93CH-4973142). This cuts against the timing and is reflected in the small size.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-11 Corning entered a $2.0B at-the-market equity program with Goldman Sachs (8-K plus 424B5, 'general corporate purposes'), and the stock fell about 14% the next session. The Q3 release and 10-Q will show whether shares were sold at the September-October prices of roughly $125-165. What the money buys is answered and corroborated: about $2B of 2026 capex rising through H2 for optical, a 10x US connectivity capacity expansion with NVIDIA, and LTAs with Amazon, Meta (up to $6B), AT&T (>$3B, 2026-09-29), Verizon, Lumen and Zayo, with some customers prepaying to reserve capacity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ATM announcement itself cost about 14% on 2026-09-14. No prior print has disclosed ATM usage.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is fully priced (a 14% drop on a facility under 2% of market cap). Only the usage figure is new, and at most 1.5-2% dilution is immaterial to EPS. Funding a contracted capacity ramp is a zero, not a negative.
findings.independence: The CFO at Citi said customers are 'providing cash to support capacity expansions and reserve production' (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/corning-sees-20b-run-rate-040200542.html). The Q2 release documents the NVIDIA and Amazon agreements (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24741/000002474126000253/glw-20260728xex99xq22026.htm).

findings.finding: Industry price trackers report single-mode G.652D/G.657 fiber prices rising through 2026, with roughly a 10% increase reported around June 2026 on top of large increases since mid-2025 and lead times of 6-12 months on AI data-centre demand. This supports Optical Communications pricing and margin ($2.07B in Q2, +32% YoY, net income +77%), though Corning is mostly on LTAs with 'value-based pricing'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Optical has been the line this stock trades on. Q2 optical +32% with net income +77% still met a 12.1% fall.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy from vendor blogs with no September-October datapoint, and the fiber shortage narrative is widely reported, so the effect is mostly priced. It is filed small as macro-to-company transmission. The CFO also said Corning is 'not fiber-constrained today'.
findings.independence: Futu reports Q2 optical profit up 77% on fiber shortages (https://news.futunn.com/en/post/1001579791/fiber-optic-shortages-drive-77-surge-in-corning-s-glwus). That is the company's own number, a different source.

findings.finding: GLW enters the print inside an AI-infrastructure rout: -19% in October, -15.8% over 20 days, -50% from the June peak. On 2026-10-16 the Nasdaq fell 2.1% on concerns about 'the unsustainability of investment levels in the AI infrastructure space' and CoreWeave's capex obligations, with TSMC's cautious note on 2027. GLW fell 8.3% on 2026-10-22 on a JPM target cut. The hyperscaler capex prints that would settle the debate are not in this window, so the tape stays fragile into a bmo print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-28 the stock fell 12.1% after already dropping about 46% in July from the peak, so a de-rated, washed-out tape has not prevented a sell-the-news reaction before.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: puts are bid (+4 skew) and the stock is already down 19% this month. The negative is small because short interest is low (about 2%, 2.2 days to cover), so there is no squeeze; but a trailing P/E of about 44x (about 29x 2027) still leaves room for de-rating if the guide disappoints.
findings.independence: MarketBeat on the 2026-10-22 -8.3% drop and the JPM cut (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-corning-nyse-glw-stock-falls-83-on-analyst-downgrade-2026-10-22/). Motley Fool on the 19% October decline (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/25/corning-stock-has-lost-half-its-value-since-june-is-it-a-buy-before-its-next-report/).

findings.finding: AT&T's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-21) reaffirmed more than 40M fiber locations by end-2026 and more than 60M by 2030, kept 2026 capital investment at $23-24B, and set 2027-28 at $22-23B a year. The carrier side of Corning's optical demand from its largest telco partner is steady, with no acceleration. Carrier is the minority of Optical (enterprise grew 65% in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Carrier softness was questioned on the Q2 call (first-half carrier +17%). It has not been the driver of print-day moves.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a counterparty that spoke after Corning last did. It confirms rather than changes the carrier run-rate, and the $3B Corning-AT&T supply agreement (2026-09-29) locks volume, so it is neutral.
findings.independence: Fierce Network on the AT&T-Corning $3B deal (https://www.fierce-network.com/broadband/corning-bags-3b-fiber-supply-deal-att).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management expected handheld units down mid-teens for the full year because of memory prices, with Gorilla Glass outperforming but still down. At Citi the CFO repeated that consumer electronics and automotive are softer. This is a drag on Glass Innovations/Specialty that is inside the Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Consumer electronics has not been the line this stock moved on in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Guided and public, so it is almost fully priced. It matters only net of optical, which is about 44% of sales and growing above 30%.
findings.independence: The Quartr summary of Citi 2026 notes handheld weakness from memory shortages (https://quartr.com/events/corning-incorporated-glw-citi-s-2026-global-tmt-conference_oz31tiOU).

findings.finding: Solar (Hemlock plus wafer) had sales of $438M in Q2 (+90%) with a $7M net loss after a maintenance shutdown, and management expects profit to improve from Q3. The CFO cited a Section 232 ruling supporting polysilicon pricing and solar reaching corporate-average profitability by end-2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Solar has been a secondary line, never the driver of a print-day move.
findings.why_not_priced: The improvement is guided. Only the pace of the swing to profit is open.
findings.independence: CFO at Citi 2026-09-09 on the Section 232 ruling (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/corning-sees-20b-run-rate-040200542.html).

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive, on the Q4 display price hike and a possible margin target. That cuts mildly against the +4 put skew and the -16% 20-day slide, but the name's four straight sold beats, including one after a 46% drawdown, keep p_up near 50 and leave the downside paid in options as a defensible stance.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells its beats): Q3-at-high-end finding cut from +0.5 to +0.2.
Lesson 6 (bar unsourced for Q4): the Q4 consensus is only implied, so the display price-hike guidance finding was capped from +1.0 to +0.7 and the margin-target finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4.

Core step 4, no double application: the draft's positioning finding (-1.0) mixed the reaction history already applied to the Q3 finding with the October AI tape, so it was resized to the tape alone at -0.5.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): fiber-price finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2; solar cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the ATM funds a corroborated capacity ramp (LTAs, prepayments, $2B capex), so it stays at 0, not negative.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (about 2%, 2.2 days to cover), no squeeze adjustment needed; the negative tape finding agrees with the skew.
Added an insider-selling finding at 0 for breadth; p_up and abs_move_pct unchanged (52, 8.0).
